## Hands-on 5 – The preregistration {#the-preregistration-moment}

::: {.none}
1. Open the preregistration block in your report
2. Complete fields 1–5: the claim, the data-in-hand statement, your one specification, the one-sentence justification from your DAG, and your rule for what supports or undermines the claim
3. **Render**, or on the browser lab page copy the completed cell into your notes
4. Type **"declared"** in chat – then wait for the class
:::

::: {.fragment}
Nobody runs a model until everyone in the class has completed their preregistration block.
:::

::: notes
We preregister together, because a thing that the whole class does at once sticks in a way that an instruction does not. Open Task 5. Fill in the five fields: the claim, the data-in-hand statement, your one specification with an option for each of the fourteen decisions, the one-sentence justification that your graph gives you, and the rule – written now, before any result – for what would support the claim and what would undermine it. The data-in-hand statement is where you record what you already know about the data before you fix your specification. Render the report; the rendered file with its timestamp is the dated record of your preregistration, like the frozen snapshot that the OSF keeps of a registration. On the browser lab page, copy the completed cell into your notes. Then type "declared" in chat, and wait. [count them in aloud: "eight declared… twelve…"] Nobody runs anything until the whole class is in. And if the specification you choose is one that you already tried in Task 4, that is allowed, but say so in the block, because a specification whose result you have already seen is not preregistered in the strict sense.
:::

## Hands-on 5 – The preregistered run {#run-it-then-watch-the-chart .smaller}

::: {.small}
- **Task 5** – run the specification in your preregistration, and only that one
- `report_result()` prints a one-click link to the Google Form with your results already in it – click, submit
- Your dot joins the **Multiverse** page as a *declared* result (the name that the chart gives to a preregistered specification), beside the exploratory ones from Task 4
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Compare the two waves. If the preregistered dots fall systematically to one side of the exploratory ones, it is worth discussing why.
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Stuck? Type "STUCK" in the chat; reload and rerun; try a second browser; follow my screen; as a last resort, your specification is one row of the curve, which the download button on the Multiverse page serves with its *t* and df
:::

::: notes
Go. Run the specification in your preregistration, just that one, and when the numbers are in front of you call report underscore result: it prints a link to the Google Form with your values already filled in, one click and you have submitted. Your dot joins the chart as a declared result, which is the name that the chart gives to a preregistered one, and it appears beside the exploratory dots that the class submitted in Task 4. If the preregistered dots fall systematically to one side of the exploratory ones, that tells you something about what people chose to preregister once they had tried the alternatives, and it is worth a conversation. If anything misbehaves: type STUCK in chat and work down the ladder on the cheatsheet. And if your machine is truly finished for the day, your specification is one row of the curve, which the download button on the Multiverse page serves with its t and its degrees of freedom, and I will help you submit it by hand. Everybody gets a dot on the chart, no exceptions.
:::
